la:noun:motus.html:
mōtus, ūs, m.
moveo
,
a moving, motion (freq. and class.).
Lit.
In gen.: orbes, qui versantur contrario motu,: deus motum dedit caelo,: natura omnia ciens et agitans motibus et mutationibus suis,: motus astrorum ignoro,.—Poet.: futuri,departure,: sub Aurorae primos excedere motus,: crebri terrae,i. e. earthquakes,; .—
In partic., artistic movement, gesticulation, dancing: haud indecoros motus more Tusco dabant,gesticulated,: Ionici,dances,: Cereri dare motūs,to perform dances, dance,: palaestrici,the motions of wrestlers,. —Of the gestures of an orator, .—Of military movements, evolutions: ut ad motūs concursūsque essent leviores,.—
Transf., a stage in the growth of a plant: tres esse motūs in vite, seu potius in surculo, naturales: unum quo germinet: alterum quo floreat: tertium quo maturescat,.—
Trop.
In gen., of the mind or heart, a movement, operation, impulse, emotion, affection, passion, agitation, disturbance (syn.: affectus, perturbatio): cum semper agitetur animus, nec principium motus habeat,: motūs animorum duplices sunt, alteri cogitationis, alteri appetitūs,: motūs animi nimii, i. e. perturbationes,: mentis meae,: animi motus et virtutis gloriam esse sempiternam,: tres quae dulcem motum afferunt sensibus,sensation,: Manto, divino concita motu, impulse, inspiration, .—
In partic.
A political movement, sudden rising, tumult, commotion.
In a good sense: Italiae magnificentissimus ille motus, Cic. pro Dom. 56, 142.—
Rebellion, sedition: omnes Catilinae motūs conatūsque prohibere,: motum afferre rei publicae,: populi,: servilis,a rising of the slaves, insurrection,: motum in re publicā non tantum impendere video, quantum tu aut vides, aut ad me consolandum affers,a change, alteration,.—
In rhet., a trope (= immutatio verborum, Cic.), ; cf. .—
A motive (post-Aug.): audisti consilii mei motūs,.
